laws.title: City flower
laws.content:
The flower known by the botanical name of "Nerium," commonly known as Oleander, is hereby declared to be the official flower of the city and as such may be displayed in the streets and parks of the city, and otherwise appropriately used.

(Code 1956, § 1-7)
laws.plain: Oleander is New Orleans' official city flower, and the city may use it to decorate streets and parks.

laws.title: Horizontal drains within buildings
laws.content: All horizontal drains shall be provided with cleanouts located not more than 100 feet (30.48 m) apart, except that the maximum shall be 50 feet (15.25 m) for drains 4 inches (100 mm) diameter or less, 150 feet (45.7 m) for drains 10 inches (250 mm) diameter or larger.
laws.plain: A building's horizontal drain pipes must have cleanout access points no more than 100 feet apart. That spacing tightens to 50 feet for pipes 4 inches wide or smaller, and loosens to 150 feet for pipes 10 inches or larger.

laws.title: Business Regulations, Business Taxes, Permits and Licenses
laws.content:
(2-2004)

Such persons, when so operating, shall display on the front of their person the identification card issued to them by the San Diego Police Department, and shall, in any case, exhibit said identification card on demand of any peace officer.

*(Amended 9–25–1989 by O–17357 N.S.)*
laws.plain: While working, these people must wear the ID card issued by the San Diego Police on the front of their body, and must show it to any officer who asks.

laws.title: Expiration date and renewal requirements
laws.content:
(a) A license that is issued under this division shall expire on April 30th of each year.

(b) A business license that is issued under this division shall remain valid until the expiration date unless suspended or revoked in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, Licenses.

(c) A business license that is issued under this division may be renewed only by submitting a completed application and paying the required fee as provided for in this division.

(d) All applications for renewal of a license that is issued under this division shall be filed before May 1st of each year.

(Code 1984, §§ 6-5-28, 6-7-28; Ord. No. 04-04, § 1(6-5-28), eff. 2-17-2004; Ord. No. 06-17, § 1(6-7-28), eff. 4-20-2017)
laws.plain: Licenses under this section expire every year on April 30 and stay valid until then unless suspended or revoked. To renew, file a completed application and pay the fee before May 1 each year.

laws.title: § 5-102. Commissioner's duties
laws.content:
The Commissioner of Health is responsible for:

(1) inspecting all property in the City, as the Commissioner considers necessary or appropriate to discover nuisances; and

(2) requiring the removal of all nuisances so discovered.

*(City Code, 1976/83, art. 11, §§101, 102(1st cl.); Ord. 99-548)*
laws.plain: The city Health Commissioner must inspect property as needed to find nuisances, and must order anything found to be removed.

laws.title: Management of municipal courts parking lot
laws.content:
The department shall have and exercise management of the municipal courts parking lot, being that parking lot bounded by Lubbock, Reisner, West Capitol, and Houston Avenue. The department shall collect and account for the revenues therefrom.

Users of the municipal courts parking lot shall be liable for payment of the fees stated for this provision in the city fee schedule, including sales tax, per vehicle.

(Ord. No. 08-568, § 26, 6-18-08; Ord. No. 2010-304, § 5, 4-21-2010, eff. 4-1-2010; Ord. No. 2011-1168, § 13, 12-14-2011)

Note—Formerly § 2-438.

Secs. 2-509—2-520. Reserved.
laws.plain: The department runs the parking lot bounded by Lubbock, Reisner, West Capitol, and Houston Avenue and collects the money from it. People who park there pay the posted fee plus sales tax per vehicle.

laws.title: § 19-2703. Nonconforming Luminaires and Lighting Systems. [Ord. 1631, 8/14/2000, Section III]
laws.plain: Outdoor lights installed before this ordinance can stay even if they no longer meet the rules. You may keep maintaining and repairing them, like changing burned-out bulbs or fixing broken parts, but if you replace or expand them, the new work must follow the current rules.

laws.title: Title 33, Planning and Zoning
laws.plain: A detached garage qualifies only if it sits at least 50 feet from the front property line (25 feet from a side street on a corner lot), is no bigger than 24 by 24 feet, is under 15 feet tall with walls under 10 feet, has no living space, and its dormers meet the setback rules.

laws.title: Hau’ula and Ka’a’awa Rural Community Commercial Centers
laws.content:
- Architectural Style
  - Encourage and support new building construction, existing building renovation or site redevelopment in a manner which complements and conveys the surrounding area’s rural character.

- Site Design
  - Utilize landscaping within the parking lot and along the center’s Kamehameha Highway frontage in order to soften its appearance and improve its compatibility with the community’s rural character.
laws.plain: New construction, renovation, and redevelopment in these rural commercial centers should match the area's rural character, and parking lots should use landscaping along Kamehameha Highway to soften their appearance.

laws.title: Plumbing Permits NOT Required Under This Code
laws.content:
The following equipment or systems do not require the issuance of permits in accordance with this Code provided such equipment or systems are installed in accordance with manufacturers requirements and applicable state and federal laws regulating such installation:

For repairs which involve only the working parts of a faucet or valve, the clearance of stoppages, the repairing of leaks where such repairing does not require the replacement of more than five feet of pipe, the replacement of defective faucets or valves or the removal. For repair of appliances already permitted may be made without permit provided no alterations are made in the existing piping fixtures.
laws.plain: Some minor plumbing work needs no permit, as long as it follows the manufacturer's instructions and state and federal law: repairing the working parts of a faucet or valve, clearing clogs, fixing leaks that need five feet of pipe or less replaced, swapping broken faucets or valves, and repairing already-permitted appliances without changing the existing pipes.

laws.title: License applications
laws.content:
A. Platforms. Platform licenses are issued by the Director and may be obtained by filing with the Director a platform application in a format determined by the Director.

B. Operators. Operator licenses are issued by the Director and may be obtained by filing with the Director a short-term rental operator license application in a format determined by the Director and by submitting a signed declaration of compliance attesting that each dwelling unit, or portion thereof, offered for short-term rental use satisfies the requirements of Section 6.600.070.

C. Bed and breakfasts. Bed and breakfast licenses are issued by the Director and may be obtained by filing with the Director a bed and breakfast operator application in a format determined by the Director.

D. All platform, operator, and bed and breakfast licenses shall expire one year from the date the license is issued and shall be renewed annually.

(Ord. 125490, § 1, 2017.)
laws.plain: Short-term rental platform, operator, and bed-and-breakfast licenses are all issued by the Director. You apply on the Director's form, and operators also sign a statement that each unit meets the rules. Every license expires one year after it is issued and must be renewed yearly.

laws.title: B. Applications for operating permits
laws.content: An application for an operating permit shall be in writing on a form provided by or otherwise acceptable to the Code Enforcement Officer. Such application shall include such information as the Code Enforcement Officer deems sufficient to permit a determination by the Code Enforcement Officer that quantities, materials, and activities conform to the requirements of the Uniform Code. If the Code Enforcement Officer determines that tests or reports are necessary to verify conformance, such tests or reports shall be performed or provided by such person or persons as may be designated by or otherwise acceptable to the Code Enforcement Officer, at the expense of the applicant.
laws.plain: Apply for an operating permit in writing on the Code Enforcement Officer's form, including whatever information they need to confirm the work meets code. If they require tests or reports, you must provide them at your own expense.

laws.title: Equal Protection
laws.content: In the event the town enters into a franchise agreement of any kind with any other person or entity other than the grantee, to enter into the town’s public ways for the purpose of constructing or operating a cable system or providing cable service to any part of the town, the material provisions thereof shall be reasonably comparable to those contained herein, in order that one operator not be granted an unfair competitive advantage over another, and to provide all parties equal protection under the law. (1976 Code § 5.45.210)
laws.plain: If the town later lets another company use its public ways to run a cable system, that deal must be roughly as fair as this one, so no cable operator gets an unfair advantage over another.

laws.title: § 10-32. Sale and discharge of fireworks restricted. [Code 1982, § 9.04]
laws.content: The provisions of § 167.10 Wis. Stats. regulating the sale and use of fireworks, exclusive of any penalty imposed thereby, is adopted by reference and made a part of this chapter as though set forth in full. A person convicted of violation of this section, in addition to such forfeiture as is ordered by the court, shall pay all costs incurred in regard to destruction of such fireworks, including any administrative expenses and storage costs in regard thereto as determined by the police department.
laws.plain: Marshfield adopts Wisconsin's state law on selling and using fireworks. Anyone convicted of breaking this rule must also pay all costs of destroying the fireworks, including storage and administrative costs set by the police.

laws.title: Temporary Structures
laws.content:
SECTION:

7-8-1: Shipping/Storage Containers

7-8-1: SHIPPING/STORAGE CONTAINERS:

Temporary storage containers, shipping containers, pods, or any other similar portable structure may be placed within the City Limits of Steamboat Rock subject to the following restrictions:

A. No wheels or undercarriage.

B. Placed and maintained perfectly level on a rodent proof foundation.

C. May not be used as a dwelling, living quarters, for camping, cooking, or any recreational use.

D. Must not be kept in the front setback area or designated parking areas, shall not impede traffic or pedestrians. No Temporary Portable Storage Container shall be placed or located in a circulation aisle/lane, fire access lane, public utility easement or public right-of-way, including streets, sidewalks, and parking strips.

D. Must be kept in good repair. A Temporary Portable Storage Container is not in a state of good repair when any of the following occur: incapable of being moved intact, has exposed rust, has scaling paint, unable to be secured against unauthorized entry, is not in compliance with health regulations, holes in the container exist due to damage/rot/ or rust, has been infested with vermin or o
laws.plain: You may place a storage container, shipping container, or pod in town only if it has no wheels, sits level on a rodent-proof base, isn't used for living or cooking, stays out of front setbacks, parking areas, easements, and rights-of-way, and is kept in good repair with no rust, peeling paint, holes, or pests.

laws.title: § 4.20.250. Failure to pay – Fraud
laws.content:
When any dealer fails to make any return and pay the full amount of the tax required by this chapter, there shall be imposed, in addition to other penalties provided in this chapter, a specific penalty to be added to the tax in the amount of one hundred dollars and ten percent of the tax due if the failure is for not more than thirty days, with an additional five percent for each additional thirty days, or fraction thereof, during which the failure continues, not to exceed twenty-five percent in the aggregate; but, if the failure is due to good cause shown to the satisfaction of the mayor, the return with remittance may be accepted exclusive of penalties. In the case of a false or fraudulent return, where willful intent exists to defraud the city of any tax due under this chapter, a specific penalty of fifty percent of the amount of the proper tax shall be assessed. All penalties and interest imposed by this chapter shall be payable by the dealer and collectible by the mayor as if they were a part of the tax imposed, and shall be in addition to any criminal penalty which may be imposed.

(prior code § 3.32.280; Ord. 78-17 § 3(part); Ord. 88-7 § 3(part))
laws.plain: If a business doesn't file its tax return and pay in full, it owes an extra penalty: $100 plus 10% of the tax if up to 30 days late, growing 5% for each additional 30 days, capped at 25%. The mayor can waive penalties for good cause. Knowingly filing a false return to cheat the city adds a 50% penalty, on top of any criminal penalty.

laws.title: A8.910 Withdrawal or Rollover of Drop Accounts
laws.content:
(a) Upon the termination or conclusion of a member’s participation in the DROP, the member shall be paid a lump sum equal to the balance in the member’s DROP Account, or, pursuant to the member’s instructions, that balance shall be paid as a direct rollover into a qualified retirement plan. The Retirement Board shall establish rules, and may develop such forms as may be appropriate, regarding distribution of the DROP Account proceeds, the rollover of such proceeds into a qualified retirement plan, and the time periods within such which distributions may be made.

(b) Upon the voluntary withdrawal of a member from the DROP, or the expiration of their participation period, the member shall be deemed to be retired on a service pension and shall then commence receiving directly the monthly service pension amount calculated pursuant to Section A8.903, including any cost of living adjustments to which the member would have been otherwise entitled during the time of their participation in the DROP, and shall, for all other purposes under this Charter and state law be deemed to be a retired member of the Police Department.

(Added by Proposition B, Approved 2/5/2008)
laws.plain: When you leave the DROP program, you get your account balance as a lump sum or roll it into a qualified retirement plan. After that you're treated as retired and start collecting your monthly police pension, including the cost-of-living raises you'd have earned during the program.

laws.title: Payment in Lieu of Other Taxes
laws.content:
In consideration of the franchise payments herein above provided for, it is expressly understood and agreed by the company and the Village that these payments shall be in lieu of any and all other franchise, license, occupation, or other forms of Excise or Revenue Taxes based upon or measured by the revenues, employees, payroll, property, facilities or equipment of the company, excepting, however, General Ad Valorem Property Taxes, special assessments for local improvements and Sales or Gross Receipts Taxes (all hereinafter referred to as "excepted taxes"). The franchise payments shall continue only so long as the company is not prohibited from making the payments by any lawful authority having jurisdiction in the
premises. Furthermore, if the Village does levy, charge or collect or attempt to levy, charge or collect any other franchise, license, occupation or other form of Excise or Revenue Taxes of the type above specified in this paragraph (other than excepted taxes), the obligation to make franchise payments hereunder shall be abated to the extent such other taxes are levied, charged or collected by the Village. (Ord. 376, 7-11-2017)
laws.plain: The company's franchise payments replace any other franchise, license, or revenue taxes the Village might base on the company's revenue, payroll, or property. Regular property taxes, special assessments, and sales taxes still apply. If the Village charges one of those other taxes anyway, the franchise payment drops by that amount.

laws.title: Rights of WAY
laws.content:
SECTION:

8-7-1: Driveway Approaches

8-7-1: DRIVEWAY APPROACHES:

There is hereby adopted, as a formal mandatory policy for driveway approaches the following manual: “Use of Public Right of Way Standard Approach Policy”. Said manual is produced by the Local Highway Technical Assistance Council of 1334 Grace Street, Boise, Idaho 83703-5836, this being the 1995 Edition.

This policy manual shall be followed for all driveway approaches of all types that may be designed and built within the City in the future.

The City Clerk shall keep at least three (3) copies of said policy manual on file in the City Hall at all times. (Ord. 701, 7-7-1997)
laws.plain: The city adopts the 1995 “Use of Public Right of Way Standard Approach Policy” manual as its mandatory rules for building driveway approaches. All future driveways must follow it, and City Hall keeps at least three copies on file.

laws.title: Addition of Section 123 of 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Special Inspectors Registration
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds Section 123, Special Inspectors Registration, to the 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, which provisions were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

123 SPECIAL INSPECTORS REGISTRATION

123.1 Certificate of Registration required. It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of or to act in the capacity of a special inspector for an insurance company under Rules 75, 79, and 81 of the Michigan Boiler Rules, being R408.4075, R408.4079, and R408.4081 in the Michigan Administrative Code, as promulgated by the Director of the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 4 of the Michigan Boiler

CD8:174
laws.plain: Detroit adds a registration rule to the state mechanical code: you can't work as a special inspector for an insurance company under the state boiler rules unless you hold a certificate of registration.

laws.title: Fees
laws.content:
The fees charged by the department of public works for a tour planner license shall be as follows:

(1) **Category 1 Tour Planner Licenses**:

a. Initial license issuance and annual renewal: $500.00.

(2) **Category 2 Tour Planner Licenses (Tour Company)**:

a. Initial license issuance and annual renewal: $1,000.00.

(Code 1956, § 12-236; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 1, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27526, § 2, 9-14-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 1, 3-11-21)
laws.plain: A tour-planner license costs $500 a year; a tour-company license costs $1,000 a year, for both the first license and each renewal.

laws.title: Boundaries
laws.content:
The boundaries of the Briarcliff Plaza Landmark District shall be as shown on the official zoning map adopted herewith entitled "Briarcliff Plaza Landmark District."

(Ord. No. 2017-64(17-O-1449), § 3, 11-6-17)
laws.plain: The boundaries of the Briarcliff Plaza Landmark District are whatever is drawn on the official zoning map adopted with this ordinance.

laws.title: Chapter 23.66 provisions apply
laws.content:
All property located in International District Mixed (IDM) zones is subject to the use and development standards of the International Special Review District, Chapter 23.66, in addition to the use and development standards contained in this Chapter 23.49. If there is a conflict between the use and development standards of this Chapter 23.49 and the provisions of the International Special Review District, the provisions of Chapter 23.66 apply.

(Ord. 123589, § 39, 2011; Ord. 112303 § 3(part), 1985.)
laws.plain: Property in International District Mixed (IDM) zones must follow the International Special Review District rules in Chapter 23.66 on top of this chapter's rules. If the two conflict, the Special Review District rules win.

laws.title: Transitional provisions; violations continue
laws.content:
Any violation of Ordinance No. 390-G, as amended, being the Official Zoning Ordinance of the City of Detroit, which was repealed on the effective date of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived, will continue to be a violation under this chapter and be subject to penalties and enforcement under Article V of this chapter, unless the use, development, construction, or other activity complies with the provisions of this chapter.

(Code 1984, § 61-1-11; Ord. No. 11-05, § 1(61-1-11), eff. 5-28-2005)
laws.plain: Anything that violated the old zoning ordinance still counts as a violation under this new chapter and can still be penalized, unless it now complies with the new rules.

laws.title: C. The parking demand analysis must show a need for parking at this location. The analysis must show that the following criteria are met
laws.plain: To justify parking here, an analysis must show real demand: at least 65% of it comes from uses within 750 feet, and if spaces are reserved for specific businesses, the reserved plus existing spaces can't exceed that business's maximum allowed parking.

laws.title: Charitable solicitation by municipal employees and/or agents
laws.content:
(a) No nonprofit corporation, group, or organization may engage, suffer or permit any employee or agent of the city to engage in a solicitation of funds on its behalf that requires the issuance of a class A certificate under this article unless such certificate has been issued to the nonprofit corporation, group, or organization in compliance with this article.

(b) No employee or agent of the city shall engage in a solicitation of funds on behalf of a nonprofit corporation, group, or organization that has not received a valid class A certificate issued pursuant to this article.

(c) An employee or agent of the city engaged in the solicitation of funds on behalf of a nonprofit corporation, group, or organization may solicit funds while standing in a roadway as authorized by Section 552.0071 of the Texas Transportation Code.

(Ord. No. 05-1346, § 1, 12-7-05)
laws.plain: A nonprofit can't have a city employee or agent collect donations for it unless the nonprofit holds a valid Class A certificate, and no city employee may collect for a nonprofit that lacks one. They may solicit while standing in a roadway only where state law allows.

laws.title: § 5-5. Applications
laws.content:
(a) The application for a variance must be submitted to the Planning Department and, to the greatest extent possible, must comply with the provisions of this Division I.

(b)

(1) The Planning Department must notify the applicant, in writing:

(i) of the increased premium rates for flood insurance; and

(ii) that construction below the level of the base flood increases risks to life and property.

(2) This notification must be maintained as part of the record required in § 5-7 {"Record of variance actions"} of this subtitle.

(City Code, 1976/83, art. 7, §7(e), (f); 2000, art. 7, §5-5; Ord. 88-188; Ord. 11-516; Ord. 14-208)
laws.plain: A flood-zone variance application goes to the Planning Department and should follow this division's rules. The department must tell the applicant in writing that flood-insurance premiums will rise and that building below the flood level increases risk, and must keep that notice on file.

laws.title: Commercial towing vehicle – Daily report required
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of every person operating a commercial towing vehicle for hire in the city to prepare and deliver to the superintendent of police every day, before noon, a legible and correct report, on a form prescribed by the superintendent, of every motor vehicle picked up or towed by such operator from any public way in the city during the preceding twenty-four hours. The report shall contain the date upon which the towing service was performed, the locations from and to which the vehicle was towed, the name and address of the owner of the towed vehicle, the name and address of the person requesting the towing service, the name and license number of the chauffeur, if the vehicle was chauffeur-driven, and the make, type, state registration number, city wheel tax license emblem number, engine number and serial or factory number of the towed vehicle. This section shall not apply to any person operating a towing vehicle exclusively for the purpose of towing vehicles owned by such person.

(Added Coun. J. 7-12-90, p. 18634; Amend Coun. J. 12-12-07, p. 16793, § 4)
laws.plain: Every commercial tow-truck operator must file a report with the police superintendent each day before noon listing every vehicle towed from a public street in the past 24 hours, with details like dates, locations, the owner, who requested the tow, the driver, and the vehicle's ID numbers. It doesn't apply to towing your own vehicles.

laws.title: Zones
laws.content:
(2) Development that would be located within Safety Zone 1 (runway protection zone); or

(3) Development that would exceed a Federal Aviation Regulations Part 77 airspace protection surface and for which the FAA requires marking and lighting.

(c) The avigation easement document shall be recorded with the County Recorder to provide the following as applicable:

(1) Allowance for noise exposure associated with adopted noise contour and aircraft overflight; or

(2) The right of flight in the airspace above the property in accordance with adopted airspace protection and aircraft overflight maps, which may include:

(A) Limiting the structure height and trees as applicable to help reduce or avoid potential obstructions to aircraft overflight;

(B) Permitting the airport operator access to the property for the removal or aeronautical marking of objects exceeding the established height limit; and

(C) Prohibiting electrical interference, glare, and other potential hazards to aircraft flight from being created on the property.

("Requirement for Avigation Easement" added 10-25-2011 by O-20047 N.S.; effective 1-1-2012.)

(Amended 12-17-2021 by O-21380 N.S.; effective 1-16-2022.)

Ch. Art.
laws.plain: Certain development near the airport, in the runway protection zone or tall enough to need FAA marking, must record an avigation easement with the County. The easement allows aircraft noise and overflight and can limit building and tree height, let the airport remove or mark obstructions, and ban glare or interference that endangers aircraft.

laws.title: § 13-11.9 Installation, maintenance, and repair of publication dispensing enclosures, spaces, and inserts
laws.content:
(a) It shall be the responsibility of the city to install, maintain, and repair the publication dispensing rack enclosures, either directly, by contract with a private contractor or through a special improvement district. Any cost for the installation, maintenance, and repair of the enclosure shall be borne by the city.

(b) It shall be the responsibility of the permittee to maintain any publication dispensing rack space for which it holds a permit. Any cost to maintain the space shall be borne by the permittee.

(c) It shall be the responsibility of the permittee to maintain in good operating order and repair any publication dispensing rack insert inserted into a space in a publication dispensing rack enclosure.

(d) Failure of a permittee to comply with either subsection (b) or (c) constitutes grounds for the suspension or revocation of the permit.

(1990 Code, Ch. 29, Art. 11, § 29-11.9) (Added by Ord. 02-10; Am. Ord. 14-7)
laws.plain: The city installs, maintains, and repairs the newspaper-rack enclosures at its own cost. The permit holder must maintain its own rack space and keep its rack insert in good working order. Failing to do so can get the permit suspended or revoked.

laws.title: § 4.20.250. Failure to pay – Fraud
laws.content:
When any dealer fails to make any return and pay the full amount of the tax required by this chapter, there shall be imposed, in addition to other penalties provided in this chapter, a specific penalty to be added to the tax in the amount of one hundred dollars and ten percent of the tax due if the failure is for not more than thirty days, with an additional five percent for each additional thirty days, or fraction thereof, during which the failure continues, not to exceed twenty-five percent in the aggregate; but, if the failure is due to good cause shown to the satisfaction of the mayor, the return with remittance may be accepted exclusive of penalties. In the case of a false or fraudulent return, where willful intent exists to defraud the city of any tax due under this chapter, a specific penalty of fifty percent of the amount of the proper tax shall be assessed. All penalties and interest imposed by this chapter shall be payable by the dealer and collectible by the mayor as if they were a part of the tax imposed, and shall be in addition to any criminal penalty which may be imposed.

(prior code § 3.32.280; Ord. 78-17 § 3(part); Ord. 88-7 § 3(part))
laws.plain: If a business doesn't file its tax return and pay in full, it owes an extra penalty: $100 plus 10% of the tax if up to 30 days late, growing 5% for each additional 30 days, capped at 25%. The mayor can waive penalties for good cause. Knowingly filing a false return to cheat the city adds a 50% penalty, on top of any criminal penalty.

laws.title: § 18-71. Bulk and density standards. [Ord. No. 1240, 11-13-2012]
laws.content:
(1) All developments shall comply with the standards listed for each zoning district in Article II, except as noted in this chapter.

(2) The conversion of any accessory building into a dwelling so as to accommodate an increased number of dwelling units or families shall be permitted only within a district in which a new building for similar occupancy would be permitted under this chapter.

(3) Additions or conversions of any accessory building into a dwelling shall comply with the requirements governing new construction in such district, including minimum lot size, lot area per dwelling unit, building of lot coverage, dimensions of yards and other open spaces, and off-street parking.
laws.plain: All developments must meet the zoning district's standards. Turning an accessory building into housing is only allowed where a similar new building would be, and such conversions must meet the same rules as new construction (lot size, yards, parking, and so on).

laws.title: Notice to Abate
laws.content: Upon discovery of any junk motor vehicle or junk machinery stored upon private property within the corporate limits of this city in violation of section 5-5-8 of this chapter, the mayor or a peace officer shall within ten (10) days notify in writing the owner of said motor vehicle (who is the owner or person in control of the property upon which it is stored) that: a) the motor vehicle constitutes a nuisance under the provisions of this chapter; b) that the owner must remove or repair the motor vehicle or machinery in accordance with the terms of section 5-5-10 of this chapter; and c) that failure to remove or repair the motor vehicle or machinery will be sufficient cause for its removal by the city at the owner’s cost. (1975 Code)
laws.plain: If a junk vehicle or junk machinery is found stored on private property against the rules, the mayor or a police officer has 10 days to notify the owner in writing that it's a nuisance, that they must repair or remove it, and that the city can otherwise haul it away at the owner's expense.

laws.title: § 217-19. Installation of parking pay station
laws.content: In all parking meter zones, the Lake Placid Village Board may cause parking pay stations to be installed upon the area controlling parking provided in this article. In areas where parking is controlled by parking pay station, it shall be illegal for any vehicle to park in violation of this chapter. Each vehicle must pay for and display an unexpired parking payment receipt. The Chief of Police shall be responsible for the regulation, control, operation and use of such parking pay station. Each device shall be so set to produce a parking payment receipt upon the deposit of the appropriate payment, indicating the date, hour and minute through which the vehicle displaying such receipt may continue to legally park and, upon expiration of the parking payment receipt, the right of such vehicle to park shall cease and the operator, owner, possessor or manager thereof shall be subject to the penalties hereinafter provided.
laws.plain: The Village can install parking pay stations in metered zones. Where one is in use, you must pay and display an unexpired receipt, and parking in violation is illegal. The Police Chief oversees the machines, which print a receipt showing how long you may park, after which your time is up and you can be fined.

laws.title: § 9-701. Nuisances Prohibited. [Ord. 1387, 9/8/1992, Section 701]
laws.content: No person shall cause or permit to exist, upon land which she/he owns or occupies under lease, license or agreement of sale, any nuisance whatsoever including, but not limited to, the accumulation of refuse or fecal matter; the outside storage of junk automobiles; improperly operated or located compost piles; the burning or emission of contaminants into the open air without a permit; the growth of noxious vegetation; the maintenance of any dangerous structure which is unfit for human habitation; or the harboring or housing of a barking dog(s) or other animal creating a noise which is offensive to a person of normal sensibilities.
laws.plain: You can't create or allow a nuisance on property you own or occupy. That includes piled-up trash or waste, junk cars stored outside, bad compost piles, burning or releasing pollutants into the air without a permit, noxious weeds, dangerous buildings unfit to live in, or a barking dog or other animal making offensive noise.

laws.title: Vagrancy
laws.content:
The following persons shall be deemed guilty of committing the crime of vagrancy:

A. Every person begging food, money, drinks, lodging or other things, or soliciting charity for himself or dependents.

B. Every person who lodges in or about any marketplace, shed, railroad car, outhouse, lavatory, rest room, warehouse, barn, service station, school, bar, cocktail lounge, or any other place of business or structure within the town, without the permission of the owner or party entitled to possession thereof. (1976 Code § 9.16.020)
laws.plain: Under this old ordinance, a person is guilty of vagrancy if they beg for food, money, drink, lodging, or charity for themselves or dependents, or if they sleep in places like markets, sheds, railroad cars, restrooms, barns, gas stations, schools, or bars without the owner's permission.

laws.title: Shielding
laws.content: Except as otherwise provided, or in subsection 8-3-1B of this chapter, all outdoor luminaires shall be shielded in such a manner that light rays emitted by the luminaire, whether directly from the lamp or indirectly from the luminaire, are restricted to regions below an angle fifteen degrees (15°) beneath the horizontal plane running through the lowest point on the luminaire where light is emitted. No significant intensity of light shall be emitted from the luminaire horizontally, nor above the horizon, nor above the region defined above. In general, all outdoor lighting shall be downward directed, except where specified otherwise in this chapter. (Ord. 331, 3-8-2005)
laws.plain: Outdoor lights must be shielded so their light only goes downward, staying below 15 degrees beneath the horizontal line at the lowest point where light comes out. No strong light may shine sideways or upward. In general all outdoor lighting must point down unless the chapter says otherwise.

laws.title: Violations; Penalty for Disregarding Notices or Orders
laws.content:
The owner of any dangerous building who shall fail to comply with any notice or order to repair, vacate or demolish said building given by any person authorized by this Chapter to give such notice or order shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. Each and every day such failure to comply continues beyond the date fixed for compliance shall constitute a separate offense.

The occupant or lessee in possession who fails to comply with any notice to vacate and who fails to repair said building in accordance with any notice given as provided for in this Chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. Each and every day such failure to comply continues beyond the date fixed for compliance shall constitute a separate offense.

Any person removing the notice provided in subsection 4-6-4J of this Chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. (Ord. 412, 7-8-1970)
laws.plain: An owner who ignores an order to repair, vacate, or demolish a dangerous building is guilty of a misdemeanor, and each day they don't comply is a separate offense. The same applies to a tenant who won't vacate or repair, and to anyone who removes the official notice.

laws.title: A8.420 Establishment of and Membership in Health Service System
laws.content: A health service system is hereby established. Said system shall be administered by the human resources department subject to the approval of the health service board. The members of the system shall consist of all permanent employees, which shall include officers of the City and County, of the San Francisco Unified School District, and of the Parking Authority of the City and County of San Francisco and such other employees as may be determined by ordinance, subject to such conditions and qualifications as the Board of Supervisors may impose, and such employees as may be determined by collective bargaining agreement. Any employee who adheres to the faith or teachings of any recognized religious sect, denomination or organization and, in accordance with its creed, tenets or principles, depends for healing upon prayers in the practice of religion shall be exempt from the system upon filing annually with the human resources department an affidavit stating such adherence and dependence and disclaiming any benefits under the system. The human resources department shall have the power to exempt any person whose compensation exceeds the amount deemed sufficient for self coverage and any
laws.plain: This creates the city's Health Service System, run by the human resources department under the health service board. Members are permanent city, school district, and Parking Authority employees, plus others set by ordinance or labor contract. An employee whose religion relies on prayer for healing can opt out each year by filing an affidavit and giving up system benefits, and HR can also exempt anyone paid enough to cover their own care.

laws.title: § 2-21. Minors under 16
laws.content:
It is unlawful for the proprietor or person in charge of any premises on which there is a pinball machine (as that term is described and characterized in this article), which is or should be licensed under this article, to permit any person under 16 years of age to operate that device at any time.

(City Code, 1966, art. 15, §73(1st sen.); 1976/83, art. 15, §93(1st sen.); Ord. 56-664; Ord. 99-526)
laws.plain: A place with a licensed pinball machine can't let anyone under 16 play it, at any time.
